issues.description: Docstring/code key mismatch: max_steps vs max_step, val_interval declared but never read
issues.detail: Constructor docstring promises max_steps and val_interval, but the code reads max_step (singular) and never uses val_interval. log_interval is read but unused. A user following the documented config gets a KeyError on first run. Validate the config shape once at construction and fail loudly.

issues.description: Training loop overshoots max_step and can skip final checkpoint
issues.detail: The outer while-loop in run() only checks global_step < max_step between full save_interval windows. train() runs save_interval batches unconditionally, so global_step can exceed max_step and the loop may exit without a final save. Add an inner step check and an explicit terminal save outside the loop.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats silently produces wrong values when contract isn't met
issues.detail: SUM-then-divide-by-world_size is only correct if every rank contributes a finite per-rank mean with equal weight. NaNs, empty iterators, counts, or pre-reduced values silently corrupt the result. Document the contract, assert finiteness, weight by sample count, or use ReduceOp.AVG.

issues.description: valid() averages per-batch means unweighted across variable-size batches
issues.detail: sum(values)/len(values) over per-batch means gives every batch equal weight regardless of sample/token count, materially distorting dataset-level loss/perplexity for variable-length LM data. Carry (sum, count) pairs and divide once, or weight each batch by its sample count.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery parses directory names without validation
issues.detail: int(x.name.split('step_')[-1]) accepts any directory containing 'step_' and crashes on suffixes like step_1000_best. Identity is inferred from filesystem places rather than a manifest. Use an anchored regex, reject non-matches loudly, or maintain a checkpoints.json log of (step, path).

issues.description: Explicit resume_path silently swapped for auto-discovered checkpoint when missing
issues.detail: If the user passes resume_path but the path doesn't exist, the code silently falls back to the latest checkpoint in output_dir with no warning. Running a different checkpoint than the operator requested is hostile. Log a loud warning or refuse to proceed.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a NEEDS-WORK verdict centered on two structural problems: the trainer_args contract is broken (docstring says max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and ignores val_interval), and the training loop's stop/validate/save schedules share one counter that overshoots max_step and can skip the final save. The distributed reduction in _all_reduce_stats and the per-batch validation averaging both silently produce wrong numbers under unstated preconditions (equal-weight batches, finite values, per-rank means). Checkpoint identity is inferred fragilely from directory names rather than a manifest, and an explicit resume_path is silently swapped when missing. None of this is hard to fix, but the docstring/key mismatch and loop-termination bugs must land before merge.
